rv.q: This gently enjoyable show deserves to find an audience — and will surely enchant Baby Boomers nostalgic for the sounds of the Sixties.
It’s a funny kind of musical in which the leading performance feels like a massive redeeming feature, rather than part and parcel of what makes the show special.
But the show lacks the drama that some of us still hunger for in a musical.
I did feel the earth move under my feet, but I’m pretty sure it was just the Piccadilly Line running below.

cn.t: Critics find this jukebox musical efficiently delivers Carole King's greatest hits, though the biographical book lacks depth. Katie Brayben's star-making performance wins praise, but the show prioritizes nostalgia over insight.
